transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I guess I came in because I just don’t have the push I used to. I used to go to choir, do my quilting, visit people, things like that. Now most days I just sit at home with the TV on low, even when I know folks are expecting me somewhere.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
I don’t know if I’d call it depressed. I’m not crying all the time or anything. I just feel kind of… flat, I guess. Like it’s hard to get myself going.
Do you still enjoy things when you do them?

Not like I used to, no. If I do make it to choir or sit down with my quilting, I can get through it, but it doesn’t pull me in the same way. Mostly I just end up staying home with the TV low, even when I know people are waiting on me.
Have you been having trouble with your memory?
Not that I’ve really noticed. I mean, I forget little things here and there, but nothing that feels different to me.
Have you been feeling sad most days?
I don’t think I’d say sad most days. It’s more like I just don’t feel much one way or the other. I have quiet days, but not really sad like that.
Have you been worrying a lot lately?
No, I don’t think I’ve been worrying a lot. I mean, I think about things some, but not more than usual.
How long have you been feeling this flat and having such a hard time getting yourself going?
I guess it’s been a little over two years now. It kind of started building after I retired from the school office.
Did these changes start after you retired?
Yes, I think so. It started after I retired from the school office, and it’s just kind of built up since then. That was a little over two years ago.
During these past two years, was there ever a period when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks?
I’m not really sure. I’ve felt kind of flat for a long time, but I don’t know that I’d say depressed most of the day every day like that.
Do you feel this change in yourself started because of retiring?
I don’t know if it was because of retiring exactly. It did seem to start around then, but I can’t say for sure that’s what caused it.
Over these past two years, have you felt this flat way on most days?

Yes… most days, I’d say. It’s like I just don’t have the push I used to. I used to go to choir, work on quilting, visit people, but now I mostly sit at home with the TV on low, even when I know folks are expecting me.
Lately, have you been feeling that you’re not worth much or that you’ve let yourself down?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get disappointed in myself sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I feel like I’m not worth much.
Have you been feeling hopeless?
No… I don’t think I’d call it hopeless. I get tired of how things are sometimes, but I’m not sitting there thinking there’s no point or nothing can get better.
At any point in the last two years, did you lose your appetite?
I don’t think so. My eating’s been pretty much the same, as far as I can tell.
In the last two years, was there ever a time when you felt depressed nearly all day, almost every day, for two weeks or longer?
No, I don’t think so. I’ve had down days, but not nearly all day every day like that for two weeks.
Do you feel your retirement has been the main reason you’ve been feeling this way?
Yes, I think it has a lot to do with it. It’s been building since I retired from the school office, a little over two years ago.
Would you say this has gone on longer than you expected after retiring?
Yes, I would. I thought I’d settle into it after a while, but it’s been kind of building since I left the school office, and that was a little over two years ago.
Do you feel you’ve adjusted to retirement yet?
Not really, no. I thought I would have by now, but it’s been kind of building since I retired from the school office, a little over two years ago.
Has this change been causing problems in your day-to-day life?

Yes, it has. I’ve had to step back from leading the choir and from helping with some of the senior-center projects. I just don’t keep up with what I said I would do. And my church friends check on me more now than they used to, so I think they notice it too.
Have you been feeling low on energy?

Yes. I just don’t have the push I used to. Things like choir, quilting, even going to visit folks… I know I should, and I know people are expecting me, but most days I end up sitting at home with the TV on low.
